chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) [regarding] the Statement of the Blessed and Exalted:
'And they swore by Allah with the most energetic of their oaths: Allah will not raise up him who dies. Yea! it is a promise binding on Him, quite true, but most people do not know.'

He said: Then he said to me, 'O Abu Baseer! What do you say about this Verse?' I said, 'The polytheists are alleging and swearing to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) that Allah does not resurrect the dead.'
He said: Then he said, 'Woe unto those who say this. Ask them: Did the polytheists swear by Allah or by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, enlighten me.'

He said: Then he said to me, 'O Abu Baseer! When our Rising One (Al-Qaim) makes the stand, Allah will send to him a group from our Shiites with the sheaths of their swords upon their shoulders. So that will reach a group from our Shiites who did not die. They will say: So-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so have been resurrected from their graves and they are with Al-Qaim. So that will reach a group from our enemies. They will say: O group of Shiites, how you lie! This is your government and you are speaking lies about it? No, by Allah, those have never lived and they will not be living until the Day of Judgement.'
He said: Then Allah quoted their words, saying: 'And they swore by Allah with the most energetic of their oaths: Allah will not raise up him who dies.'

key_terms.الرجعة: Al-Raj'ah: the belief in the return of certain believers before the Day of Resurrection, a distinctive Shia doctrine
key_terms.القائم: Al-Qaim: 'The Rising One,' a title for the Twelfth Imam al-Mahdi (ATFS) who will establish justice
key_terms.اللات والعزى: Al-Lat and Al-Uzza: pre-Islamic Arabian idols worshipped by the Quraysh and other Arab tribes
key_terms.جهد أيمانهم: With the most energetic/binding of their oaths — denotes the strongest oath possible

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of Quran 16:38 about swearing by Allah that the dead will not be resurrected?
ai.summary: Abu Baseer narrates his dialogue with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about Quran 16:38, the verse concerning the polytheists' denial of resurrection. The Imam refutes the common interpretation (that the verse refers to mushrikeen denying resurrection to the Prophet) by pointing out that the mushrikeen swore by their idols, not by Allah. The Imam then reveals the true interpretation: the verse foretells the enemies of the Ahlulbayt who, during the era of Al-Qaim's rise, will deny the miraculous return (Raj'ah) of deceased Shi'a who are resurrected to stand with him — and Allah has quoted their denial in advance.
